items.dir: Directions: You have just finished a course taught by a foreign teacher. Write a letter to him or her to express your gratitude. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
ol: 说明写信目的，感谢一学期的教导
具体说明哪一点帮助最大（如口语纠音、写作批改）
表达祝愿，希望保持联系
fr: 第一段：点明身份与写信目的——课程结束，写信致谢
第二段：举一个具体事例说明收获，避免空泛赞美
第三段：再次感谢，表达祝愿与保持联系的愿望
items.es:
Dear Mr. Smith,

I am Li Ming, a student from Class Three. Now that the oral English course has come to an end, I am writing to express my sincere gratitude for your teaching over the past term.

What impressed me most was the way you corrected my pronunciation. In the first weeks, I was afraid to speak in class because my accent made me nervous. You listened patiently, wrote the problem sounds on the board and asked me to practise them in short dialogues. Thanks to your encouragement, I can now give a presentation without reading every word.

Your class has made English a habit rather than a subject for me. I will keep reading and speaking every day. I wish you all the best in your future work, and I hope we can stay in touch by email.

Yours sincerely,
Li Ming
ph: express my sincere gratitude for ... 对……表示诚挚感谢
What impressed me most was ... 给我印象最深的是……
Thanks to your encouragement ... 多亏你的鼓励
stay in touch with sb. 与某人保持联系

items.es:
Dear Professor Brown,

I am Wang Fang, chair of the Student Union of the Foreign Languages School. On behalf of our school, I am writing to invite you to the Chinese Culture Festival, which will be held in the Student Centre from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 20 May.

The festival will include calligraphy workshops, a tea ceremony and a short stage performance. Since you have studied Chinese poetry for many years, we would be honoured if you could give a ten-minute talk on how poetry reflects everyday life. Your talk would give students a fresh view of the culture they are learning about.

Please let me know whether you are available by 10 May so that we can arrange the seating and the schedule. We sincerely hope you can join us.

Yours sincerely,
Wang Fang

Two points may make me a suitable candidate. items.es:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am a junior student who studies in the library almost every day. I am writing to report a problem that has become serious during the exam period.

In the reading room on the third floor, students often discuss their group projects at normal speaking volume, and some watch videos without earphones. Last Tuesday I sat there for three hours but finished only half of my reading. Several classmates have moved to the canteen, which is far from ideal for quiet study.

I would suggest setting aside one room for group discussion and putting up reminder signs at the entrance of the silent area. It would also help if staff walked through the reading room once every hour.

I hope these suggestions will be considered, and I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Zhang Wei

items.es:
Dear President,

I am a sophomore writing to share some thoughts on the campus canteen. I would like to begin by thanking the staff, whose work has clearly improved since the new menu was introduced last term.

Two problems, however, still affect daily life. First, the queue at the second-floor window is often twenty minutes long between 12:00 and 12:30, which leaves little time for a short rest before afternoon classes. Second, vegetarian dishes are limited to one or two options, so students with special dietary needs often eat the same meal for a week.

May I suggest opening an extra window during peak hours and adding two vegetarian dishes each day? A simple online menu would also help students decide before they queue.

Thank you for your time, and I trust the canteen will continue to improve.

Yours sincerely,
Chen Jing

Dear Professor Liu,

I am writing to apologize for damaging the book you kindly lent me last month, A Short History of Modern Europe.

On Friday I carried it in my backpack during a rainstorm. The bottom of the bag was wet, and about twenty pages at the back are now wrinkled. I only noticed the damage when I opened it in the library. I should have put it in a plastic folder, and I am sorry that I did not take better care of something you trusted me with.

I have ordered a new copy, which should arrive early next week. I will bring it to your office as soon as it comes, and I am also happy to pay for any difference in price. I promise to be more careful with borrowed materials in the future.

Yours sincerely,
Zhao Lei

What distinguishes her, however, is her willingness to explain difficult problems to others. Before last term's final exams, she organised four review sessions and prepared summary sheets for the whole class. As a result, no one in our study group failed the course.

She is also reliable. When our group project lost a member halfway through, she took over the missing part without complaint and finished it on time.

I believe she deserves the scholarship and recommend her without reservation.

He Xin

Dear Ming,

I saw the news on the university website this morning: first prize in the national English speech contest. Congratulations! I read the report twice to make sure I had not mistaken the name.

I still remember the evenings in March when you practised in the empty classroom. You recorded yourself, listened to the playback and rewrote the same opening five times. There were days when you almost gave up because your pronunciation would not cooperate, but you came back the next morning. The prize is not luck; it is the result of those months.

I hope this gives you the confidence to try even bigger stages. When you are back on campus, let's have dinner and celebrate properly.

Yours,
Tao

items.es:
Dear Freshmen,

I am a senior who passed CET-6 last December. Since many of you have asked how to prepare, I would like to share three suggestions.

First, treat vocabulary as a daily habit rather than a task before the exam. Twenty words a day for three months is far more effective than two hundred words in one week. Second, do real papers under timed conditions. Reading three passages in forty minutes feels very different from reading them without a clock. Third, keep a notebook of mistakes: after each paper, write down why you chose the wrong option, not just the correct answer.

Finally, do not panic if your first mock score is low. Progress in listening and reading is slow at the beginning and then suddenly visible. Give the method eight weeks before you judge it.

Good luck,
Xu Ming

items.ti: 大学是否应强制体育课
items.dir: Directions: Some people believe physical education should be compulsory for all university students. Others think students should decide for themselves. What is your opinion? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 提出争议，给出明确立场
论述强制体育课的两个理由
承认自由选择的价值，但说明为何不足以替代
fr: 第一段：引入争议，明确赞成强制
第二段：理由一（健康习惯）+ 理由二（公平与基础技能）
第三段：让步 + 重申立场
items.es:
Should university students be required to take physical education? In my view, a compulsory course is justified, provided that it offers real choices.

The first reason is habit. Most students arrive with irregular sleeping hours, and few will voluntarily add exercise to a crowded timetable; a required class gives them a fixed weekly slot. The second is fairness: free facilities sound generous, but those who already play well use them most.

Opponents argue that adults should manage their own time. That is reasonable in principle, yet the evidence from many campuses is that optional programmes attract mainly the already active. Compulsory does not mean uniform, so I would keep the requirement and let students choose the sport.

Therefore, required physical education, with flexible options, serves students better than pure freedom.
ph: provided that 只要（引导条件状语从句）
in practice 实际上
sound generous 听起来慷慨
That is reasonable in principle, yet ... 原则上合理，然而……

items.ti: 人工智能会取代教师吗
items.dir: Directions: Some argue that artificial intelligence will replace teachers in the near future. To what extent do you agree? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明 AI 能替代的部分与不能替代的部分
fr: 第一段：部分同意，但整体否定「取代」
第二段：AI 的优势（个性化练习、即时反馈）与其局限
第三段：教师不可替代的职能 + 结论
items.es:
Will artificial intelligence replace teachers? I agree that it will take over part of their work, but the claim that it will replace them goes too far.

AI is genuinely useful where practice must be repeated. It can generate unlimited exercises, mark grammar mistakes instantly and adjust the difficulty to each learner. A teacher with forty students cannot do this at three in the morning. Yet learning is not only the transfer of information. A good teacher notices that a quiet student has stopped asking questions, or that a joke has hurt someone. These judgements depend on relationship and context, which no model currently reads.

Moreover, students learn how to argue by watching someone argue with them fairly. An algorithm can produce counter-arguments, but it cannot care whether the student is convinced.

The likely future is cooperation: AI handles routine practice and feedback, while teachers spend more time on motivation, discussion and guidance. Teachers will change, not disappear.
ph: goes too far 说得过头了
take over 接管、接手
the transfer of information 信息传递
The likely future is cooperation 未来很可能是协作

items.dir: Directions: Some universities ban mobile phones in classrooms. Do you think this is a good policy? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明禁令的合理性与执行难点
fr: 第一段：有条件支持禁令
第二段：注意力成本 + 执行中的问题
第三段：给出更细的方案（分场景）
items.es:
Should mobile phones be banned in classrooms? I support a partial ban, but not a blanket one.

A phone on the desk reduces attention even when it is silent, and one student's notification distracts the whole row. In large lecture halls, the cost of a single glance is a lost paragraph of explanation. However, a total ban is difficult to enforce fairly. Teachers cannot inspect every bag, and rules that are widely broken teach students to ignore rules in general.

In seminars and labs, phones can stay in bags; in lectures where students take notes digitally, they may be used openly. Some instructors already ask everyone to place phones face down at the corner of the desk for the first ten minutes, which is easy to check.

The goal is not to punish devices but to protect attention. A clear, limited and consistently applied rule does that better than an absolute ban.
ph: a blanket ban 一刀切禁令
The case for ... is strong ……的理由很充分
face down 面朝下
consistently applied 一致执行的

items.dir: Directions: Some people say anonymity online does more harm than good. To what extent do you agree? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明不完全同意，需区分场景
匿名保护的价值（举报、求助、少数群体）
匿名的代价及分层治理
fr: 第一段：不同意「弊大于利」的整体判断
第二段：举出匿名不可替代的价值
第三段：承认代价 + 提出分层方案
items.es:
Does online anonymity do more harm than good? I do not think the question can be answered with a single judgement, because anonymity protects some speakers and shields others.

Anonymity has real value. Employees who report safety problems, patients discussing rare diseases and students asking questions they fear are stupid all depend on it. In many cases, requiring a real name would silence exactly the people whose voices are most needed. At the same time, anonymity lowers the cost of abuse. Insults, threats and coordinated harassment spread faster when no one can be identified.

The sensible response is not to abolish anonymity but to make it accountable. Platforms can require verified identity at registration while displaying only a nickname, and they can suspend accounts whose behaviour is repeatedly reported. Readers can also be given tools to see an account's history.

Anonymity is a tool, not a virtue. Its value depends entirely on the rules that surround it.
ph: do more harm than good 弊大于利
silence exactly the people ... 恰恰让最需要发声的人沉默
make it accountable 让它可追责
a tool, not a virtue 是工具，不是美德

items.ti: 毕业后去大城市还是小城市
items.dir: Directions: Some graduates prefer to work in large cities, while others choose smaller cities. Which do you think is a better choice? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明选择取决于阶段与目标

第二段：大城市的优势与成本

items.es:
Where should graduates start their careers: a metropolis or a smaller city? I believe the answer depends on the stage of one's career rather than on a general ranking of cities.

Large cities concentrate opportunities. In media, finance and technology, one district may hold more employers than an entire province, and changing jobs does not require moving house. The cost is equally concentrated: rent takes a third of a beginner's salary, and commuting consumes two hours a day.

Smaller cities offer a different bargain. Housing is affordable, commuting is short, and a capable graduate may be given responsibility earlier than in a large firm. However, the range of employers is narrow, and a bad match is harder to escape.

My suggestion is to treat the first three years as a learning period. Start where the learning curve is steepest, then decide where to settle once the trade-offs are clear.
ph: concentrate opportunities 集中机会
a fair trade 一笔公平的交易
a different bargain 另一种交易
where the learning curve is steepest 学习曲线最陡的地方

items.dir: Directions: Some students take a gap year before university. Do you think this is a wise choice? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 间隔年能解决的具体问题
fr: 第一段：有条件赞成
第二段：间隔年带来的两项收益（方向感、独立性）
第三段：风险与前提（计划、经济、期限）
items.es:
Is a gap year before university a wise choice? It can be, but only when it is planned rather than simply postponed.

A year of work, volunteering or travel can supply what school does not: a sense of what daily work actually feels like. Someone who spends six months assisting in a hospital ward learns more about whether she wants to be a doctor than any brochure can teach. Living away from parents also builds practical independence — managing a budget, dealing with a landlord, cooking.

The risks are real. A year without structure can become a year of scrolling, and the habit of study is easy to lose. Costs also vary enormously: travel requires money, and paid work may leave little time for reflection.

Therefore, a gap year should have a written plan, a budget and a fixed end date. With these conditions, it is an investment; without them, it is only a delay.
ph: planned rather than simply postponed 是有计划的，而非单纯推迟
supply what school does not 提供学校给不了的东西
The risks are real. 风险确实存在。
an investment ... a delay 是投资……是拖延

items.ti: 纸质书会被电子书取代吗
items.dir: Directions: Some people believe printed books will disappear as e-books become more popular. Do you agree? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 电子书的优势与使用场景
纸质书不可替代之处，结论为并存
fr: 第一段：不同意「消失」
第二段：电子书的效率优势
第三段：纸质书在深度阅读与记忆中的作用 + 结论
items.es:
Will printed books disappear? I doubt it. What we are seeing is a division of labour rather than a replacement.

E-books are better for certain purposes. A student can carry hundreds of titles on one device, search a term across a library and read in the dark. For reference works and guides, the electronic form is cheaper.

Printed books, however, do something that screens do not. Studies of reading comprehension repeatedly find that people remember the structure of a long argument better on paper, partly because the position of a passage on a page becomes a memory cue. A physical book also invites undivided attention: there are no notifications at the edge of the page. That is why many students who read articles online still buy paper copies of the books they need to think with.

Printing may shrink, but it will not vanish. The two forms will serve different needs, and readers will be the better for having both.
ph: a division of labour rather than a replacement 是分工而非取代
a memory cue 记忆线索
invite undivided attention 让人专注
be the better for 因……而受益

items.dir: Directions: University rankings are widely used but also widely criticised. What is your view? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 承认有限价值，指出主要问题
排名的问题：指标偏差、激励扭曲
fr: 第一段：有限有用，但不能当作唯一依据
第二段：问题一（指标偏研究）+ 问题二（激励扭曲）
第三段：使用建议（分专业、看细分指标）
items.es:
Are university rankings meaningful? They are useful as a rough guide and dangerous as a final answer.

Their value lies in comparison. For a student who knows nothing about foreign institutions, a ranking provides a starting list and some information about research output. But the indicators are not neutral: most weight goes to publications and citations, which favour large science-heavy universities and say little about teaching.

When a number becomes a target, institutions may recruit international students for the statistics rather than for the classroom, or split research into smaller papers to raise counts. Students then pay for a figure that measures something other than their education.

The sensible use is narrow: compare programmes rather than universities, look at subject-level tables, and treat the overall rank as one data point among many. A ranking can open a door, but it cannot tell you whether you will learn well behind it.
ph: as a rough guide 作为粗略参考
indicators are not neutral 指标并非中立
When a number becomes a target ... 当数字变成目标……
one data point among many 众多数据点之一

items.ti: 志愿服务是否应纳入必修
items.dir: Directions: Some universities make volunteer service a graduation requirement. Do you agree with this practice? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 必修能带来的覆盖与公平
强制的风险与设计要点
fr: 第一段：总体赞成，但需设计得当
第二段：两个理由（覆盖面、打破圈层）
第三段：风险（形式化）+ 设计建议
items.es:
Should volunteer service be a graduation requirement? I support the idea, provided that the requirement is designed around real work rather than a signature.

The main argument for compulsion is coverage. If service is optional, it attracts students who are already motivated; a requirement brings in those who would never have tried, and some discover an interest they did not know they had. Service also puts students in contact with people outside the campus.

The risk is formalisation. When hours are counted, some students will find the easiest way to collect them: taking a photo, signing in and leaving. To avoid this, the requirement should be tied to a specific project with a supervisor, and assessment should be based on a short reflection rather than on the number of hours.

Compulsory service is defensible only if it produces genuine contact. Otherwise it teaches students to treat community work as paperwork.
ph: provided that 只要
tends to attract 往往会吸引
be tied to 与……挂钩
treat A as B 把 A 当作 B

items.dir: Directions: Some people think entertainers are overpaid. Others argue that their incomes reflect market demand. Discuss both views and give your opinion. Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 市场逻辑的合理性与局限
给出自己的判断与调节方式
fr: 第一段：引出争议
第二段：市场观点 + 其局限（稀缺性被放大、外部性）
第三段：我的判断：收入本身不应设上限，但税收与分配需调节
items.es:
Are entertainers paid too much? The debate usually opposes fairness to freedom, but the two are less opposed than they appear.

Those who defend high incomes point to demand: a film that sells a billion tickets can afford to pay its lead actor well. The limitation is that attention markets are winner-takes-all, so the gap between the first and second performer reflects distribution technology as much as talent.

Critics reply that a nurse and an actor cannot be compared. That is true, but it does not follow that a salary cap is the answer; caps are easy to evade and hard to justify in a market economy.

My view is that the income itself is not the problem. The problem is what happens after it: if tax rules allow the highest earners to pay proportionally less, the sense of unfairness is justified. Progressive taxation and transparent contracts address the issue more effectively than moral criticism.
ph: winner-takes-all 赢家通吃
as far as it goes 就其本身而言
It does not follow that ... 并不能由此推出……
progressive taxation 累进税制

items.dir: Directions: Some universities teach major courses entirely in English. Do you think this is a good practice? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 风险（理解深度、师生负担）与前提
fr: 第一段：有条件支持
第二段：收益（文献获取、国际交流）
第三段：风险与前提（师资、分层、过渡）
items.es:
Should major courses be taught entirely in English? I support the practice for advanced courses, but not as a blanket rule for every subject.

Taught well, English-medium instruction removes a barrier. In computer science and economics, most current papers appear in English first, and a student who has discussed them in class can read the literature without translating every paragraph. It also prepares students for conferences and for international workplaces.

The risk is shallow learning. When both the subject and the language are new, students may understand the words but miss the argument. Weaker listeners quietly give up and rely on slides. A second problem is teacher supply: a lecturer who is brilliant in Chinese may become hesitant in English, and the loss is borne by students.

The condition, therefore, is support. Universities should train teachers, allow bilingual materials in the first year, and evaluate courses by what students actually learn rather than by the language on the timetable.
ph: English-medium instruction 全英文授课
removes a barrier 消除障碍
The loss is borne by students 代价由学生承担
by the language on the timetable 以课表上的语言来评判

items.ti: 博物馆是否应免费开放
items.dir: Directions: Some people argue that museums should be free of charge. Do you agree? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
fr: 第一段：赞成，但需解决经费
第二段：免费的三重价值（可及性、随机参观、公共属性）
第三段：成本与替代方案（政府拨款、特展收费、捐赠）
items.es:
Should museums be free? I believe they should, because a museum is closer to a public library than to a cinema.

The strongest argument is access. A ticket price of forty yuan is trivial for a middle-class family and decisive for a student or a retired worker. Free entry also changes behaviour: people drop in for half an hour, return to see one room properly, and bring visiting relatives. Charging by visit encourages a single exhausting tour instead.

There is, of course, a cost. Buildings, staff, insurance and conservation must be paid for. But the choice is not between free and bankrupt. Several models work: public funding covers core costs, temporary exhibitions charge separately, and shops and cafés generate income. Donations can be invited without being demanded.

A society that keeps its collections behind a price tag teaches people that culture is a luxury. Free entry, supported by stable public funding, teaches the opposite.
ph: is closer to A than to B 更像 A 而不像 B
trivial for ... decisive for ... 对……微不足道，对……却是决定性的
drop in 顺道来访
behind a price tag 藏在价签之后

items.ti: 是否应限制私家车进城
items.dir: Directions: Some cities restrict private cars in the city centre. Do you think this is a reasonable policy? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 赞成限制，但需替代方案
限制的理由（拥堵、污染、空间效率）
fr: 第一段：赞成，前提是公共交通到位
第二段：三条理由
第三段：公平问题 + 配套（公交、停车换乘、豁免）
items.es:
Should cities restrict private cars in the centre? I think restriction is reasonable, but only where public transport can absorb the trips that cars no longer make.

The case rests on space. A single lane of road can move about 2,000 cars an hour, or up to 20,000 bus passengers. When a city centre dedicates most of its street space to cars, it is using its scarcest resource inefficiently. Restrictions also cut pollution at street level, where pedestrians and shopkeepers spend their days, and reduce the noise that makes ground-floor housing unattractive.

The fairness objection deserves an answer. A ban that falls on everyone hurts those who cannot afford to live near the centre or to change cars. Exemptions for residents, delivery vehicles and disabled drivers, together with park-and-ride schemes and frequent buses, make the policy bearable.

Restriction is not a punishment for drivers. It is a decision about what a street is for.
ph: absorb the trips 承接这些出行
The case rests on ... 理由在于……
The fairness objection deserves an answer. 公平性异议值得回应。
what a street is for 街道是为什么而存在

items.dir: Directions: Online courses have become common. Some say they can replace face-to-face classes. Do you agree? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 网课的优势与适用场景
线下课不可替代的部分
fr: 第一段：否定「替代」，主张混合
第二段：网课优势（可回看、跨地域、自定进度）
第三段：线下课的不可替代性（节奏、互动、责任感）+ 结论
items.es:
Can online courses replace face-to-face classes? They can replace some of them, but not the part that matters most.

Online courses have genuine advantages. A recorded lecture can be paused and replayed, which helps students whose first language is not the language of instruction. Geography stops mattering too: a student in a small town can attend a course given by a specialist a thousand miles away.

What the screen struggles to reproduce is rhythm and obligation. In a room, a teacher reads confusion in five faces and slows down; a seminar forces each student to speak, and the awareness that one must speak is itself a form of learning. Deadlines set by a person whom you will meet on Thursday carry more weight than a timestamp on a platform.

The sensible arrangement is blended learning: lectures online, discussion and laboratory work in person. The question is not which mode is better, but which tasks belong to which.
ph: the part that matters most 最重要的部分
Geography stops mattering. 地理位置不再重要。
carry more weight than 比……更有分量
which tasks belong to which 哪种任务属于哪种模式

items.dir: Directions: Some people encourage university students to start businesses while studying. Others think students should focus on their studies. Discuss both views and give your opinion. Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明两种观点各自的道理
创业的教育价值与风险
fr: 第一段：呈现两种立场
第二段：创业的价值（真实反馈、能力）+ 风险（时间、资金、失败成本）
第三段：我的判断：支持小规模试错，反对盲目投入
items.es:
Should university students start businesses while they are still studying? Both camps have a point, and the disagreement is really about scale.

Supporters argue that a small venture teaches faster than a classroom. A student who tries to sell a product discovers within weeks whether anyone wants it. Critics reply that a start-up consumes the time that should go into a degree, and that most student businesses close within a year, leaving debts and missed courses.

My view is that the two positions can be reconciled by size. A project that can be run in ten hours a week, with little capital and a clear stop date, is educational. Borrowing money or delaying graduation to chase an idea is a different decision, and it should not be encouraged by policy or by fashion.

Learning to build something is valuable; risking everything to prove it is not.
ph: Both camps have a point 双方都有道理
the disagreement is really about scale 分歧其实在于规模
Failure at twenty-two is cheaper than ... 二十二岁失败比……代价小
reconcile A by B 通过 B 调和 A

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing why many university students stay up late and what can be done about it. You should write 120 to 180 words.
fr: 第一段：现象描述，给出具体场景
第二段：原因（作息惯性、宿舍环境、屏幕）
第三段：影响 + 建议
items.es:
Walk through any dormitory at one in the morning and you will still see screens glowing. Late sleeping has become normal among university students, and the reasons are not simply laziness.

Three causes stand out. The first is a timetable mismatch: classes may start at eight, but the most productive hours for many young people are late at night, when the corridor is finally quiet. The second is the dormitory itself. One student's keyboard clicks and another's video call keep everyone awake, so the whole room drifts later together. The third is the phone, which offers endless short videos that make stopping feel like a decision rather than a default.

The effects are cumulative: poor concentration in morning classes, irregular meals and lower immunity. Simple countermeasures help more than lectures on willpower — switching off the main light at eleven, agreeing on quiet hours, and charging phones outside the bed.
ph: stand out 突出、显眼
drift later together 一起越睡越晚
make stopping feel like a decision 让「停下来」变成一个需要决定的事
countermeasure 对策

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the popularity of short videos and its effects on young people. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 描述短视频的普及程度
fr: 第一段：现象与规模
第二段：吸引力（即时反馈、低门槛、算法）
第三段：双面影响 + 建议
items.es:
Short videos have become the default way to fill a spare minute. On buses, in queues and between classes, the same gesture appears: thumb down, thumb up, repeat.

The attraction is well designed. Each clip delivers a complete reward in fifteen seconds, which is short enough to avoid boredom and long enough to feel satisfying. Production is cheap, so anyone can appear. Above all, the recommendation system learns quickly; after a few swipes it knows which topics hold your attention, and the next clip is always slightly better than the last.

The effects run both ways. Short videos spread practical knowledge fast — a cooking technique or a grammar point can reach millions in a day. But they also train attention to expect constant novelty, making a forty-page chapter feel unbearably slow.

The useful response is not abstinence but boundaries: a fixed time, a place where the app is not installed, and one long task finished before the first clip.
ph: the default way to fill a spare minute 填补空闲时间的默认方式
The attraction is well designed. 吸引力是被精心设计的。
run both ways 有两面性
not abstinence but boundaries 不是戒断，而是设边界

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the growing number of students applying for postgraduate study. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析原因（就业门槛、专业兴趣、缓冲）
fr: 第一段：现象描述
第二段：三重原因
第三段：隐忧（盲目跟风、资源错配）+ 建议
items.es:
The number of students sitting the postgraduate entrance examination has risen for most of the past decade, and in some provinces it now exceeds the number of undergraduates graduating.

Three forces are at work. Employers increasingly use a master's degree as a filter, so a bachelor's certificate buys fewer interviews than it did ten years ago. Some students genuinely want to go deeper into a subject; a third group uses the examination as a buffer against a discouraging job market.

There is nothing wrong with any of these motives, but the third deserves scrutiny. A degree taken only to delay adulthood can leave graduates older but no clearer about their direction, and it adds to the mismatch between training and demand.

The sensible question before registering is not what others are doing but what the degree will let you do that you cannot do now.
ph: Three forces are at work. 有三股力量在起作用。
buys fewer interviews 换来更少的面试机会
deserves scrutiny 值得审视
no clearer about their direction 对方向并没有更清楚

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing why more urban households keep pets and what problems need attention. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析原因（独居、情感需求、消费）
fr: 第一段：现象与规模
第二段：原因（居住形态、情感补偿、社交媒体）
第三段：问题（弃养、扰民、医疗）+ 建议
items.es:
Pets have moved from the courtyard into the apartment. In many Chinese cities, the number of registered dogs and cats has grown faster than the number of households.

The reasons are partly structural. Smaller families and later marriages mean more people live alone, and a dog provides a routine and a reason to go outside. Emotional need is the second factor: a pet offers company without the complications of human relationships, and for elderly residents it may be the main daily conversation. Social media has amplified the trend by making pet ownership look like a lifestyle rather than a responsibility.

The problems are equally visible. Abandonment rises after holidays, barking disputes occupy neighbourhood committees, and veterinary costs surprise new owners. Registration, mandatory vaccination and a simple licence fee would help, but the deeper need is education before purchase: a pet is a fifteen-year commitment, not a purchase to be returned.
ph: moved from the courtyard into the apartment 从院子搬进了公寓
amplify the trend 放大这一趋势
occupy neighbourhood committees 占用居委会的精力
a fifteen-year commitment 十五年的承诺

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the spread of the phrase 'lying flat' among young Chinese people. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明该说法指什么、不等于什么
fr: 第一段：界定概念，避免误读
第二段：背景（竞争强度、成本、期望落差）
第三段：评价：是信号不是方案
items.es:
The phrase 'lying flat' spread quickly among young Chinese people, and it is often misunderstood. It rarely means refusing to work; more often it means declining an extra promotion, an unpaid weekend or a competition whose prize seems unreachable.

Competition for good university places and stable jobs intensified at the same time as housing costs rose, so the distance between effort and reward widened. Many young people also grew up being told that any goal was achievable, and discovered in their twenties that this was not quite true.

As a slogan it is honest; as a plan it is weak. Withdrawing from competition may protect a person's health for a year, but it does not create the conditions for a better life.

The more useful reading is that the phrase is a signal. It tells employers and policymakers where the return on effort has become too low, and it invites them to respond.
ph: declining an extra promotion 拒绝额外的晋升
the distance between effort and reward widened 努力与回报之间的距离拉大
give that gap a name 给这种落差一个名字
the return on effort 努力的回报

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the near-total adoption of mobile payment in Chinese cities and its consequences. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 讨论被忽略的代价与补救
fr: 第一段：现象，从现金到扫码
第二段：效率、卫生、可追溯
第三段：代价（数字鸿沟、隐私、断网）+ 补救
items.es:
In most Chinese cities, paying with cash now feels unusual. From street vendors to hospitals, a QR code has replaced the note and the coin.

The efficiency gains are real. A queue moves faster when no one is counting change, small transactions become economically possible, and records are automatic, which helps both households and tax authorities. Contactless payment also reduced physical contact during the pandemic and cut the cost of handling cash.

The costs are less visible. Elderly people who cannot operate a smartphone find ordinary shopping difficult, and tourists without a local account are locked out of many services. Every payment also produces a data trail that can be used for profiling. And a payment system that depends on electricity and signal fails exactly when a crowd most needs it.

The remedy is not to reject the technology but to keep alternatives alive: cash must remain legal tender, and machines should still accept cards.
ph: street vendors 街头小贩
locked out of 被排除在外
a data trail 数据痕迹
legal tender 法定货币

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing why museums have become popular among young people. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析原因（文化认同、社交分享、产品创新）
fr: 第一段：现象，预约一票难求
第二段：三方面原因
第三段：隐忧（打卡式参观）+ 建议
items.es:
Tickets for major museums now disappear within minutes of release. A decade ago, the same institutions were quiet on weekday afternoons.

Three factors explain the change. First, cultural confidence: young visitors are less inclined to treat Western art as the default standard and more curious about their own history. Second, the visit has become social content; a well-lit exhibition hall is a good place for photographs, and sharing them signals taste. Third, museums have learned to design: creative products, themed cafés and evening openings turn a hall of objects into an experience.

The risk is that the queue becomes the point. Visitors who spend forty minutes photographing and ten minutes looking learn little, and crowded halls make deep viewing impossible.

The remedy lies with the museums themselves: timed entry, quieter routes for those who want to read labels, and exhibitions that reward attention rather than a camera.
ph: disappear within minutes of release 放票几分钟内就没了
less inclined to treat A as the default 不太会把 A 当作默认标准
turn A into B 把 A 变成 B
reward attention rather than a camera 奖励专注而非相机

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the growth of rural guesthouses in China. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 讨论同质化与社区影响
fr: 第一段：现象
第二段：需求端 + 供给端
第三段：问题（同质化、房价、社区）+ 建议
items.es:
Rural guesthouses have multiplied along the edges of cities. What began as a few converted farmhouses is now an industry with design awards and booking platforms.

On the demand side, travel habits have changed. After years of rushed sightseeing, urban families want shorter trips with slower schedules, and a two-night stay in a village fits a weekend better than a flight. On the supply side, improved roads and internet access made remote locations viable, while local governments offered subsidies to encourage renovation.

The problems appear once the model succeeds. Villages begin to look alike, with the same white walls, the same swing and the same breakfast, so price becomes the only difference. Rents rise, and young villagers may be priced out of their own community.

What sustains a destination is not decoration but distinctiveness: local food, local crafts and hosts who actually live there. Subsidies should reward that, not the number of rooms.
ph: converted farmhouses 改造过的农舍
fit a weekend better than a flight 比坐飞机更适合周末
be priced out of 因价格被挤出
What sustains a destination is ... 支撑一个目的地的是……

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the fitness boom among urban Chinese. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 讨论消费化倾向与理性健身
fr: 第一段：现象（健身房、跑步、居家训练）
第二段：健康意识、审美变化、社交平台
第三段：隐忧（办卡不练、过度消费）+ 建议
items.es:
Fitness has become a visible part of urban life. Gyms open before seven, parks fill with runners at dusk, and home workout videos collect millions of views.

The motives have shifted. Twenty years ago, exercise was mostly associated with competition or weight loss; today it is presented as a way of managing stress and energy. Health check-ups that report fatty liver or high blood pressure persuade people in their thirties, while social platforms make progress visible and therefore comparable. Cheap wearable devices add a daily number to aim at.

There is a commercial side that deserves scepticism. Annual memberships are sold on the assumption that most buyers will stop coming after February, and supplements promise results that training alone would deliver.

The healthy version of the trend is unglamorous: three sessions a week, a routine that fits the schedule, and progress measured in months rather than in purchases.
ph: collect millions of views 获得数百万播放
persuade people in their thirties 让三十多岁的人下决心
deserves scepticism 值得怀疑
unglamorous 不光鲜的

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the influence of internet slang on everyday language. You should write 120 to 180 words.
fr: 第一段：现象（口语、作文、广告）
第二段：功能（效率、认同）+ 风险（表达粗糙、语境错位）
第三段：态度：分场合
items.es:
Internet slang has moved from comment sections into classrooms, advertisements and even examination scripts. A phrase invented for a joke can become the standard way to describe an emotion within a year.

Slang does real work. It compresses a complicated feeling into two characters, which is useful in fast conversation, and it signals membership in a group. For young people, using the current word is a way of saying 'I belong here'.

The risk is a narrowing of expression. If every disappointment is described by the same word, the difference between disappointment, irritation and grief disappears. Slang also dates quickly: a phrase that sounds natural to a fifteen-year-old may sound absurd to an examiner, and using it in a formal essay costs marks.

The sensible attitude is register awareness. Slang belongs in chat and in friendly speech; formal writing requires words that will still mean the same thing in ten years.
ph: does real work 有其实际功能
a narrowing of expression 表达的窄化
date quickly 很快过时
register awareness 语域意识

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the rise of solo living among young adults. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析原因（婚育推迟、迁移、经济）
fr: 第一段：现象与规模
第二段：三重原因
第三段：影响（自由与孤独）+ 社会应对
items.es:
More young adults in Chinese cities now live alone than at any time in the past. The trend is visible in the housing market: small flats and single-room rentals are the fastest-growing segment.

Three factors drive it. Marriage and childbirth are happening later, so there is a longer period between graduation and forming a household. Internal migration separates young workers from their hometowns, and renting alone is often cheaper than sharing a flat in a convenient location. Rising incomes also make solitude purchasable, which was not true a generation ago.

Solo living has real benefits: control over time, no negotiation over housework, and space to develop habits. Its cost is loneliness, which arrives not in dramatic moments but on ordinary evenings, and which research links to poorer health.

The response should be social rather than moral. Shared kitchens, community sports and public spaces that make casual contact possible do more than advising young people to marry sooner.
ph: the fastest-growing segment 增长最快的部分
solitude purchasable 独处成为可购买的商品
arrives not in dramatic moments but on ordinary evenings 不在戏剧性时刻到来，而在普通夜晚
casual contact 随意的接触

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the popularity of second-hand trading among young consumers. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析动因（经济、环保、新奇）
讨论信任问题与规范化
fr: 第一段：现象
第二段：三重动因
第三段：问题（真假、售后）+ 建议
items.es:
Buying used has lost its stigma. Second-hand platforms now list everything from textbooks to designer bags, and a large share of their users are under thirty.

Rents and living costs take a bigger share of a young salary than for their parents, so paying half price for a desk or a bicycle is simply rational. Environmental concern is the second: a generation that has heard about carbon footprints finds it inconsistent to buy new furniture for a one-year lease. The third motive is discovery — a used item is unique, and hunting for it is entertaining in a way that a shopping cart is not.

Photographs can hide damage, descriptions can be optimistic, and returning an item to a private seller is difficult. Platforms that offer authentication, escrow payment and standard returns grow faster than those that do not.

Second-hand trading is not a temporary response to hard times; it is a more efficient use of things already made.
ph: lose its stigma 不再带有污名
take a bigger share of 占更大比例
find it inconsistent to do 觉得做某事不合逻辑
escrow payment 担保支付

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing why marathons have become popular in Chinese cities. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析参与者与城市两方面的动机
fr: 第一段：现象
第二段：个人动机（健康、目标感）+ 城市动机（形象、消费）
第三段：问题（中签难、扰民、安全）+ 建议
items.es:
A generation ago, a marathon in a Chinese city was a rare event organised for professional athletes. Today dozens of cities hold races each year, and entry places are allocated by lottery.

For runners, the appeal is a goal with a date. Training for 42 kilometres imposes structure on an otherwise flexible week, and finishing provides a sense of achievement that a gym session cannot. For cities, a race is compact publicity: roads are closed for a morning, and images of the skyline travel further than most advertising campaigns.

The problems are predictable. Residents complain about closed roads, medical staff worry about untrained runners who ignore warnings, and the lottery leaves many disappointed. Some races have also become expensive exhibitions of equipment.

Improvements are straightforward: more half-marathons for beginners, better medical screening, and routes that disturb fewer neighbourhoods. A race works when it belongs to the city, not only to the sponsor.
ph: allocated by lottery 通过抽签分配
imposes structure on 给……强加结构
compact publicity 紧凑的宣传
belongs to the city 属于这座城市

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the rise of 'national trend' consumption among Chinese young people. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析原因（设计提升、文化认同、供应链）
fr: 第一段：现象（国产运动品牌、联名、非遗元素）
第二段：三重原因
第三段：风险（符号化、溢价）+ 长期建议
items.es:
Products labelled 'national trend' now fill the shelves that foreign brands once dominated. Sneakers with embroidered patterns, tea drinks named after poems and cosmetics packaged like porcelain are bought by consumers in their twenties.

Design quality explains part of it. Chinese brands hired the same designers who once worked for international labels, and the gap in appearance closed quickly. Cultural confidence explains another part: young buyers no longer assume that imported means better, and they enjoy recognising a reference that older generations also understand. Finally, the supply chain is local, so a new idea can reach shops in weeks rather than seasons.

The risk is that the label replaces the product. When a plain T-shirt costs twice as much because of a printed character, the trend becomes a tax on patriotism, and customers notice.

The brands that last will be those whose quality survives without the label. Culture sells the first purchase; only the product sells the second.
ph: fill the shelves 摆满货架
the gap in appearance closed 外观上的差距缩小了
a tax on patriotism 对爱国情绪的征税
Culture sells the first purchase 文化带来第一次购买

items.dir: Directions: Write an essay analysing the normalisation of remote work and its effects. You should write 120 to 180 words.
ol: 分析对个人与组织的影响
fr: 第一段：现象，从应急到常态
第二段：收益（通勤、专注、地域）+ 代价（边界模糊、协作变慢）
第三段：混合模式的关键规则
items.es:
Remote work began as an emergency measure and has settled into a routine. Many companies now allow two or three days at home each week, and job advertisements list flexibility alongside salary.

The gains are clear. Removing the commute returns one to two hours a day, and those hours often go into work or sleep rather than leisure. Concentrated tasks such as writing and coding proceed faster without interruptions. Companies benefit too, because they can hire beyond commuting distance.

The costs are less obvious but real. Home and office merge, so the working day expands at both ends, and junior employees lose the incidental learning that comes from overhearing a senior colleague. Decisions that once took a corridor conversation now take three days of messages.

The hybrid model works only with explicit rules: fixed days together for discussion, clear expectations about response time, and meetings that have an agenda. Flexibility without structure becomes invisibility for those who are least assertive.
ph: settled into a routine 变成常态
incidental learning 附带的学习
corridor conversation 走廊里的对话
invisibility for those who are least assertive 对最不善表达的人而言就是被忽视

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明为何「第一步」常被高估或低估
fr: 第一段：释义，指出重点不在「千里」而在「一步」
第二段：反面现象（计划代替行动）+ 正面例子
第三段：结论，把大目标切成可执行的第一步
items.es:
Laozi's observation that a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step is often quoted and rarely practised. Its point is not that the journey is long, but that length is irrelevant until movement starts.

Most people who fail to begin do not lack ambition; they lack a first step small enough to take today. A student who plans to read fifty books this year may read none, because the plan implies a commitment that feels heavy; the same student will finish a book if this evening's task is twenty pages.

The saying also warns against a different error: treating the first step as the whole journey. Starting is easy to celebrate and hard to repeat. What produces the thousand miles is the second step, and the hundredth, taken when no one is watching.

Begin small, then keep the size of the beginning.
ph: is often quoted and rarely practised 常被引用，很少被实践
small enough to take today 小到今天就能迈出
cheap enough to survive a bad day 代价小到能在糟糕的一天里完成
treat A as B 把 A 当作 B

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Francis Bacon's saying 'Knowledge is power.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释这句话的历史语境
指出知识转化为力量的条件
fr: 第一段：解释原意（知识改变人对自然的关系）
第二段：转化条件（应用、判断、分享）
第三段：今天更需警惕「有知识无判断」
items.es:
When Francis Bacon wrote that knowledge is power, he was arguing against a view of learning as decoration. Knowledge, in his account, is power because it allows people to predict and therefore to act.

The claim needs a condition. Information stored is not power; it becomes power when it is applied to a decision. A physician who has read every paper on a disease but cannot explain a diagnosis to a frightened patient has knowledge and little power. The same is true of a student who memorises formulas without knowing when they fail.

Our era adds a new problem. Access to information has become almost free, so the scarce resource is no longer knowledge itself but judgement about which knowledge to trust. Someone who forwards a plausible chart without checking its source has more information and less power than before.

Bacon's sentence therefore remains true, but with a qualification: knowledge becomes power only when it is tested, applied and communicated.
ph: argue against a view of ... 反对把……看作……的观点
in his account 在他看来
The claim needs a condition. 这一说法需要条件。
with a qualification 附带一个限定

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'We are what we repeatedly do.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释习惯与身份的关系
举例说明习惯的复利效应
fr: 第一段：释义，习惯塑造身份
第二段：正例与反例（每天二十分钟与每天刷两小时）
第三段：改变的方法（环境设计、最小单位）
items.es:
The saying that we are what we repeatedly do, usually attributed to Aristotle, is a claim about identity rather than achievement. It suggests that character is not chosen in a single decision but accumulated in small repetitions.

Twenty minutes of reading a day is roughly twelve books a year; two hours of short videos a day is a month of waking life. Neither choice feels important on a Tuesday evening, which is precisely why the choice is important.

Willpower is a poor instrument because it is exhausted by use. Environment works better: a book on the pillow, the app removed from the first screen, a friend who expects you at seven in the morning. Starting with a unit so small that refusing it would be absurd also helps, because the difficulty of beginning is the main obstacle.

We become what we repeat, so the useful work is designing what gets repeated.
ph: a claim about identity 关于身份的主张
The arithmetic is unglamorous. 算术本身并不光鲜。
Willpower is a poor instrument 意志力不是好工具
the difficulty of beginning 开始的难度

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Bacon's line 'Reading makes a full man.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 辨析阅读与经验的关系
fr: 第一段：解释 full（知识、语言、判断）
第二段：阅读的局限，需要经验校验
第三段：如何读（带着问题、读写结合）
items.es:
Bacon's line that reading makes a full man is usually read as praise of books. It is also a description of what reading does to a mind: it supplies material that experience alone cannot provide.

A reader gains three things. The first is range: a person who has read history recognises a pattern in the news that others see as unprecedented. The second is language: sentences are learned by exposure, and a student who reads good prose begins to write differently without studying grammar. The third is judgement, though this is where the claim needs care.

Reading can also make a person full of other people's opinions. Bacon himself added that reading should be combined with discussion and writing, because material unprocessed becomes weight rather than strength.

The practical conclusion is to read with a question and to write something after reading. A book that changes no sentence you write has probably not been read, only finished.
ph: is usually read as 通常被理解为
supplies material that experience alone cannot provide 提供单靠经验无法获得的材料
this is where the claim needs care 正是在这里需要谨慎
material unprocessed becomes weight 未经处理的材料会变成负担

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Steve Jobs' advice 'The only way to do great work is to love what you do.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 指出这句话的适用边界
fr: 第一段：肯定热爱带来的投入
第二段：边界（多数人无法先热爱再选择；热爱也可后天形成）
第三段：改写这句话
items.es:
Steve Jobs told graduates that the only way to do great work is to love what you do. The advice is inspiring and slightly incomplete.

It is right about effort. A programmer who enjoys debugging will stay an hour longer than one who does not, and over a decade those hours compound.

But the sentence assumes that love comes first. For most people, work is chosen under constraints: a visa, a family obligation, a salary that must cover rent. Telling them to find their passion can turn a structural problem into a personal failure. In practice, interest often grows after competence: a person becomes good at something, is trusted with harder tasks, and begins to care.

A more honest version would be: do work you can respect, get good at it, and let affection follow. Love is often a result of mastery rather than a precondition for it.
ph: is slightly incomplete 略有欠缺
compound 累积
turn a structural problem into a personal failure 把结构性问题变成个人失败
a precondition for 的前提

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Socrates' statement 'The unexamined life is not worth living.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明反思的价值与风险
给出可操作的反思方式
fr: 第一段：释义，审视指追问依据
第二段：价值（纠错、方向）+ 风险（过度反思导致瘫痪）
第三段：方法（定期复盘、写作、他人反馈）
items.es:
Socrates' claim that the unexamined life is not worth living is a strong statement, and it is worth taking seriously without taking it literally.

To examine a life is to ask why one is doing what one is doing: whether the goal is chosen or inherited, whether the method actually works, whether the cost is acceptable. This is uncomfortable because the answers are often no. But a person who never asks will spend years optimising a route to a destination someone else selected.

Endless self-analysis can replace action, and a habit of doubting every motive produces paralysis rather than clarity. Reflection is useful when it ends in a decision and harmful when it becomes a substitute for one.

A workable version is periodic rather than constant: a monthly review of what was planned and what happened, a page of writing when a choice feels difficult, and one honest friend who will tell you what you avoid.
ph: without taking it literally 不必照字面理解
inherited 承袭而来的
optimising a route to a destination someone else selected 优化一条通往别人选定目的地的路线
a substitute for one 行动的替代品

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Edison's remark that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration. Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释这句话针对的偏见
讨论灵感与勤奋的真实关系
fr: 第一段：解释爱迪生的话针对「天赋论」
第二段：灵感并非可省略，但需积累承接
第三段：对备考者的具体启示
items.es:
Edison's remark that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration is usually quoted to encourage effort. Its sharper point is that the one percent only becomes visible after the ninety-nine.

Most people who study a field long enough produce several plausible ideas a year; what separates them is the willingness to test one, fail, and test again. The metaphor is slightly unfair to inspiration, because a good question is worth more than a hundred routine experiments. Yet good questions rarely arrive to beginners; they arrive after enough exposure for a pattern to be noticed.

Re-reading notes feels productive and changes little, because it produces familiarity rather than recall. Attempting questions, getting them wrong and correcting the errors is unpleasant and effective.

Edison's percentages need not be taken literally. The direction is what matters: effort is the part you control, and it is also the part that makes the other one percent possible.
ph: Its sharper point is that ... 更锋利的一点是……
be unfair to 对……不公平
arrive after enough exposure 在足够接触之后才出现
familiarity rather than recall 熟悉感而非提取

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the proverb 'If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明协作的代价与收益
fr: 第一段：解释谚语的两面
第二段：独行的效率与协作的复利
第三段：判断：短期独行，长期协作
items.es:
The proverb that you go fast alone and far together contains a useful distinction: speed and distance are different objectives, and they are served by different arrangements.

Decisions take minutes rather than meetings, and a single person can hold a whole problem in mind without translating it for others. This is why the early stage of a project is often best done by one person. But most substantial goals exceed one person's knowledge. A team brings different training, catches errors that its author cannot see, and continues after any individual leaves.

The cost of cooperation is coordination. Every additional member adds communication channels, and a group can spend more time agreeing than doing. That is why teams need a clear owner, a shared document and a deadline, rather than endless consensus.

My reading is that the proverb describes a sequence rather than a choice: go alone to find the direction, then go together to cover the distance.
ph: a useful distinction 一个有用的区分
hold a whole problem in mind 把整个问题装在心里
exceed one person's knowledge 超出个人知识范围
describes a sequence rather than a choice 描述的是一段顺序，而非一个选择

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Failure is the condiment that gives success its flavour.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 区分「有价值的失败」与「重复的失败」
fr: 第一段：释义，失败提供对照
第二段：有价值的失败有条件（复盘、可控代价）
第三段：方法：记录、归因、再试
items.es:
The image of failure as a condiment is appealing: without something bitter, success would taste bland. As a description of how memory works, it is accurate. People recall the exam they failed far longer than the one they passed easily.

But not every failure is nutritious. A failure becomes useful under two conditions. The first is a review: what went wrong, at which step, and what would be done differently. The second is a bearable cost: a failed course can be retaken, but a failure that consumes a family's savings teaches nothing worth the price.

The practical habit is to separate the event from the judgement. 'I did not prepare the listening section' is a fact that can be acted on; 'I am bad at English' is a verdict that cannot. The first leads to a plan, the second to nothing.

Failure flavours success only when it is digested.
ph: As a description of how memory works 作为对记忆机制的描述
nutritious 有营养的（比喻）
a bearable cost 可承受的代价
only when it is digested 只有被消化之后

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Time is the most valuable thing a man can spend.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释时间与金钱的差异
说明「花费时间」的判断标准
fr: 第一段：时间不可储存、不可再生
第二段：判断标准（不可替代性、复利）
第三段：学生的具体取舍
items.es:
The saying that time is the most valuable thing a person can spend is easy to agree with and hard to act on, because time does not feel scarce until it is gone.

Money differs from time: it can be stored, and it can be earned again. Time can do neither, so a rich person may be poor in the one currency that cannot be replenished.

If time is the currency, the question becomes how to spend it well. Two criteria help. The first is irreplaceability: some hours produce things that cannot be bought later, such as a conversation with a grandparent or the first year of a child's life. The second is compounding: an hour spent learning a language or building a habit pays again every year, while an hour of scrolling pays once.

For students, this is not an argument for constant study. It is an argument for spending the irreplaceable hours deliberately and the rest without guilt.
ph: does not feel scarce until it is gone 直到失去才觉得稀缺
This asymmetry explains ... 这种不对称解释了……
irreplaceability 不可替代性
an argument for ... 一个支持……的理由

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Tell me and I forget; teach me and I remember; involve me and I learn.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 用学习科学的视角说明原因
给出可操作的学习方式
fr: 第一段：解释从听讲到参与的递进
第二段：原因（提取练习、输出倒逼理解）
第三段：方法（讲给别人、做项目、写总结）
items.es:
The saying that telling makes us forget, teaching makes us remember and involvement makes us learn describes a ladder that most students climb too slowly.

Listening is the weakest form because it creates a feeling of understanding without testing it. Teaching is stronger: to explain something, a person must select the essential points and arrange them in order, and the gaps become obvious in the attempt. Involvement is strongest because it requires decisions under conditions that cannot be fully anticipated, which is where real understanding is revealed.

The psychology agrees. Recall practice strengthens memory more than re-reading, and explaining forces recall at the level of structure rather than detail. This is why study groups often help the explainer more than the listener.

The practical implication is uncomfortable: the activities that feel least efficient — explaining to a classmate, writing a summary from memory, solving a problem without looking at the answer — are usually the ones that work.
ph: climb too slowly 爬得太慢
the gaps become obvious 漏洞变得明显
The psychology agrees. 心理学研究也支持这一点。
The practical implication is uncomfortable 实践含义令人不适

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明简单背后的复杂工作
fr: 第一段：辨析简单与简陋
第二段：简单需要取舍与理解
第三段：在学习与写作中的应用
items.es:
The claim that simplicity is the ultimate sophistication is often misunderstood as a preference for the plain. In fact, simplicity is expensive: it is what remains after everything unnecessary has been removed.

A simple explanation is not a short one; it is one in which the reader never has to hold two contradictory ideas at once. Producing it requires the writer to understand the subject well enough to decide what to leave out, and leaving things out is harder than adding them.

The opposite of simplicity is not complexity but clutter — complexity that serves no purpose. A medical textbook is complex because the body is complex; a form with twelve unnecessary fields is merely untidy.

The lesson for students is practical. When a summary grows longer than the original, the problem is not the subject but the understanding.
ph: what remains after everything unnecessary has been removed 去掉一切不必要之物后剩下的东西
justify its place 证明自己该在这里
The opposite of simplicity is not complexity but clutter 简单的反面不是复杂，而是杂乱
grows longer than the original 比原文还长

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'The important thing is not to stop questioning.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明提问能力如何被削弱
fr: 第一段：释义，提问是认知的起点
第二段：提问能力被什么削弱（效率压力、评价体系）
第三段：方法（记录疑问、追问一层）
items.es:
Einstein's advice not to stop questioning sounds like encouragement, but it is closer to a warning. Curiosity is not a fixed trait; it is a habit that can be trained or extinguished.

A student who asks why a formula works will recognise its limits; one who only memorises it will apply it where it fails. Questions also drive the acquisition of knowledge, since an answer sticks better when it responds to something one wondered about.

What extinguishes curiosity is usually the environment. A timetable with no empty space leaves no time to follow an interest, and an examination system that rewards the correct answer punishes the interesting question. Adults are also efficient: answering is faster than exploring a doubt.

Keeping curiosity therefore requires small deliberate habits: writing questions in the margin instead of resolving them immediately, and following each answer one step further than required. The point is not to doubt everything, but to keep the door open.
ph: closer to a warning 更接近于警告
a habit that can be trained or extinguished 可以被训练也可以被消磨的习惯
responds to something one actually wondered about 回应了自己真正好奇的东西
in the margin 在页边

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Comparison is the thief of joy.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释比较为何偷走快乐
区分有害比较与有益比较
fr: 第一段：释义，比较改变注意对象
第二段：参照系问题 + 有益比较的条件
第三段：做法（与自己比、控制信息源）
items.es:
The saying that comparison is the thief of joy identifies a mechanism rather than a moral failing. Comparison does not reduce what a person has; it changes what that person looks at.

A student who has finished a difficult chapter sees a classmate's award, and the chapter stops counting. The reference group also shifts upward: once a person is surrounded by high achievers, an objectively good result feels ordinary.

Comparing your current work with your own earlier work is the basis of improvement, and comparing methods rather than outcomes can be instructive. The damage comes from comparing outcomes with people whose circumstances differ in ways the comparison ignores.

The practical response is to change the reference point and the input. Keep a record of what you did last month, and reduce the time spent on feeds that make other lives look effortless. Joy is not stolen by ambition but by a badly chosen mirror.
ph: identifies a mechanism rather than a moral failing 指出的是一种机制，而非道德缺陷
reference group 参照群体
The damage comes from ... 伤害来自……
a badly chosen mirror 选错的镜子

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Courage is not the absence of fear, but the ability to act in spite of it.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明恐惧的功能与过度
fr: 第一段：释义，勇气是带着恐惧行动
第二段：恐惧的功能（预警）与过度（瘫痪）
第三段：方法（分步暴露、预案、榜样）
items.es:
The definition of courage as acting in spite of fear is more useful than the popular image of the fearless hero, because the fearless hero does not exist in ordinary life.

Fear has a function: it warns a person before a real risk and prepares the body to respond. The problem is that the same system responds to social risk — public speaking, disagreeing with a supervisor — with the same intensity as physical danger.

Courage can therefore be trained in small steps. A student afraid of speaking can begin by asking one question in a seminar, then by presenting for three minutes, then by chairing a discussion. A written plan for the worst outcome also reduces fear, because vagueness is what makes it large.

The point is not to eliminate the feeling but to stop letting it decide. Courage is a decision made while the hands are still shaking.
ph: in spite of 尽管
responds to social risk with the same intensity 以同样的强度回应社交风险
removes the opportunity 也去掉了机会
Vagueness is what makes it large. 让它变大的正是模糊。

items.dir: Directions: Some students live in dormitories, others rent flats outside campus. Which do you think is better for university students? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 提出比较标准（成本、社交、独立性）
fr: 第一段：不宜一概而论，要看年级与专业
第二段：宿舍的优势与局限
第三段：租房的优势与风险 + 结论
items.es:
Should students live in a dormitory or rent a flat? The answer depends less on preference than on what a student needs at a particular stage.

A first-year student who lives with five others learns about different provinces, different habits and different ways of studying, and the cost of a room is often a fifth of the market rate. The limitation is control: noise, schedules and storage are shared, and a single inconsiderate roommate can ruin a term.

Renting offers privacy and a fixed routine, which matters for students preparing for a serious examination or working night shifts. It also teaches practical skills — contracts, bills, repairs. The risks are cost and isolation; a student who moves out in the first year may find that the friends were made without them.

My suggestion is therefore sequential: live in a dormitory for the first two years to build a network, then rent if a specific need appears.
ph: socially dense 社交密度高
a fixed routine 固定的作息
matters for 对……重要
live in a dormitory for the first two years 前两年住宿舍

items.ti: 读纸质书还是听有声书
items.dir: Directions: Some people prefer printed books, others prefer audiobooks. Which do you prefer and why? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明选择取决于书的类型与目的
fr: 第一段：提出按目的分工
第二段：有声书的场景优势与记忆劣势
第三段：纸质书的优势 + 我的搭配
items.es:
Printed books or audiobooks? I use both, and the choice depends on what I want from the text.

Audiobooks are excellent for certain situations. They fill the walk to the laboratory, the bus ride and the washing-up, time that would otherwise be empty. For narrative works — memoirs, popular history, novels — a good reader adds rhythm and emphasis that silent reading may miss. Their weakness is navigation: it is difficult to go back three pages to check a name, and difficult passages slide past while attention drifts.

Printed books, or their electronic equivalent, remain better for material that must be studied. Highlighting, marginal notes and the physical position of a paragraph all support memory, and the eye can move backwards as easily as forwards.

My arrangement is simple: listen to books that I could otherwise not finish, and read the ones I need to argue with. The format should serve the purpose, not become an identity.
ph: The choice depends on what I want from the text 选择取决于我想从文本中得到什么
adds rhythm and emphasis 增加节奏与重音
slide past while attention drifts 在注意力游移时滑过去
argue with 与……辩驳（指精读）

items.dir: Directions: Some students prefer large lectures, others prefer small classes. Which do you think is more effective? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明两者适合不同目标
比较大班与小班的效率差异
fr: 第一段：分别定位（知识覆盖 / 能力训练）
第二段：大班的规模优势与互动缺失
第三段：小班的深度 + 结论
items.es:
Large lectures and small classes are not competing formats; they do different jobs.

A lecture is an efficient way to deliver a framework. Three hundred students can hear a leading scholar explain how a field is organised, and the cost per student is low. The weakness is that understanding is assumed rather than checked: a student can follow every sentence and still be unable to use the idea a week later.

A small class is expensive and slower, but it forces production. When twelve people must respond to a case, silence is not an option, and the instructor can see who has misunderstood. This is where skills such as argument and analysis actually develop.

The sensible design uses both: lectures for orientation, small classes for practice. If a student must choose only one, the small class offers more per hour, because the hours spent speaking are the hours that change what one can do.
ph: do different jobs 承担不同职能
the cost per student is low 人均成本低
understanding is assumed rather than checked 理解被视为理所当然，而非被检验
offers more per hour 每小时收获更多

items.ti: 独自学习还是小组学习
items.dir: Directions: Some students study alone, others prefer group study. Which is more effective for you? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
fr: 第一段：按任务分工
第二段：独自学习的深度与小组的纠错
第三段：我的做法（先独后组）
items.es:
Studying alone or in a group? The question is poorly framed, because the two modes suit different tasks.

Understanding a difficult text requires uninterrupted time. In a group, the conversation moves at the speed of the fastest speaker, and a quiet member may leave believing she understood. Alone, a reader can stop at a paragraph for twenty minutes, which is often what comprehension requires.

Groups are better at exposing error. When you explain a concept to a classmate, the part you cannot state clearly is the part you do not know. Groups also supply pressure: a scheduled session at seven in the evening is harder to skip than a private intention.

My own arrangement is sequential. I read and take notes alone, then meet once a week to teach what I have understood. The solitary session produces the material; the group session tests it. Neither is sufficient alone, and the order matters more than the choice.
ph: The question is poorly framed 这个问题问得不好
moves at the speed of the fastest speaker 以最快者的速度推进
expose error 暴露错误
the order matters more than the choice 顺序比选择更重要

items.ti: 国内读研还是出国读研
items.dir: Directions: Some graduates pursue a master's degree at home, others go abroad. Which do you think is a better choice? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 提出判断维度（专业资源、成本、职业规划）
fr: 第一段：取决于专业与目标
第二段：出国的收益与成本
第三段：国内的优势 + 结论
items.es:
Should a graduate study at home or abroad? The answer depends on the field and on where the student intends to work.

Going abroad offers access to laboratories, libraries and supervisors that may not exist domestically, and it forces a student to operate in a second language, which is itself training. The costs are substantial: tuition, living costs, and the risk that a degree earned abroad is undervalued by employers who cannot judge the institution.

Tuition is lower, the supervisor's network is local, and internships during the programme are easier to arrange. For fields where regulation and practice differ sharply between countries — law, public administration, clinical medicine — local training is often more directly useful.

The decision should therefore follow the work, not the prestige. If the research requires equipment available only in a few places, go where the equipment is. If the career will be built domestically, choose the programme that puts you in contact with domestic employers.
ph: access to 获得……的机会
is itself training 本身就是一种训练
follow the work, not the prestige 依据工作而非名声做决定
put you in contact with 让你接触到

items.dir: Directions: Some students pursue a master's degree immediately after graduation; others work for a few years first. Which do you think is wiser? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明两种路径的适用条件
fr: 第一段：取决于是否需要先了解行业
第二段：先工作的收益与代价
第三段：直接读研的适用情形 + 结论
items.es:
Should a graduate continue studying immediately or work first? The deciding factor is whether the student knows what the degree is for.

After two years in an industry, a person knows which problems are worth studying and which credentials actually matter. That knowledge makes a master's degree more focused and often more productive. The cost is momentum: salaries rise, obligations accumulate, and returning to a student schedule becomes harder each year.

Studying first suits fields where the degree is a prerequisite rather than an upgrade — academic research, clinical practice, certain engineering specialisms. It also suits students whose undergraduate training was too general to enter the job they want.

The worst version of either path is the one chosen by default. A degree taken because one does not know what else to do delays the question without answering it, and a job taken only to avoid an examination teaches little. Choose the path that produces the information you currently lack.
ph: supplies information that no career test can provide 提供任何职业测试都无法提供的信息
a prerequisite rather than an upgrade 是先决条件而非提升手段
chosen by default 默认选择的
the information you currently lack 你当前缺少的信息

items.ti: 早起学习还是熬夜学习
items.dir: Directions: Some students study early in the morning, others late at night. Which do you think is more efficient? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 比较两种时段的学习质量
fr: 第一段：生物节律存在差异
第二段：早起的优势（干扰少、记忆巩固）
第三段：熬夜的代价 + 建议
items.es:
Early mornings or late nights? Individual body clocks differ, but the two periods are not equally good for study.

The morning has two structural advantages. Interruptions are rare, because messages and meetings arrive later. And sleep after learning supports consolidation, so material studied at night is retained better if reviewed the next morning.

Late-night study has a real appeal. The house is quiet, and there is a pleasant sense of having finally caught up. The evidence, however, is unkind: after midnight, attention and judgement decline while confidence stays high, which is why errors made at that hour are often not noticed until the next day.

A practical arrangement is to protect the first ninety minutes of the morning for the hardest task and to use the evening for review and routine work. If a student is genuinely a night person, the same principle applies: put the difficult task in the first hour after waking, whenever that is.
ph: sleep after learning supports consolidation 学习后的睡眠有助于记忆巩固
The evidence, however, is unkind 然而证据并不留情
confidence stays high 自信仍然很高
protect the first ninety minutes 守住起床后的前九十分钟

items.ti: 纸质笔记还是电子笔记
items.dir: Directions: Some students take notes by hand, others type them. Which method do you think is better? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
fr: 第一段：记笔记的两个目的（记录、理解）
第二段：手写的理解优势
第三段：电子的检索优势 + 结论
items.es:
Handwritten notes or typed notes? The answer depends on which purpose of note-taking matters more in a given class.

Notes serve two purposes: storing information and processing it. Typing is unbeatable for the first. A fast typist can record almost every sentence, and the file can be searched, reorganised and shared. The problem is that recording everything requires no thought, so the notes may be complete and the understanding shallow.

Writing by hand is slow, and the slowness is the point. Unable to copy every word, the student must decide what matters, compress it and connect it to something already known. Research on recall consistently favours this effortful selection, especially for conceptual material.

The sensible combination is to write by hand in seminars and theory classes, where the structure matters, and to type in lectures that are essentially factual, where speed and searchability matter. The tool should follow the kind of thinking the class demands.
ph: unbeatable for 在……方面无人能敌
the slowness is the point 慢正是关键
favour this effortful selection 支持这种费力的选择
searchability 可检索性

items.ti: 参加社团还是专注学业
items.dir: Directions: Some students join many student societies, others focus only on their studies. Which do you think is better? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明两者的收益性质不同
fr: 第一段：不是非此即彼
第二段：社团的不可替代收益
第三段：过度的代价 + 建议
items.es:
Should students join societies or concentrate on coursework? Framed as a choice, the question ignores that the two produce different kinds of capital.

Societies supply what classrooms rarely do: organising an event, negotiating with a venue, persuading someone who does not report to you. These experiences are difficult to acquire later and are valued by employers precisely because they cannot be taught from a textbook. A student who has run a fifty-person activity has learned something about failure that no lecture provides.

The risk is diffusion. A student in four organisations attends six meetings a week, holds two nominal titles and produces nothing substantial in any of them. The academic cost appears slowly, in the third year, when grades matter most.

A workable rule is one serious role and one light membership. Depth in a single organisation teaches more than titles across four, and it leaves enough hours for the degree that will still be on the transcript.
ph: produce different kinds of capital 产生不同种类的资本
someone who does not report to you 不归你管的人
diffusion 分散
nominal titles 名义上的头衔

items.ti: 在校兼职还是专心学习
items.dir: Directions: Some university students take part-time jobs, others spend all their time studying. Which do you think is better? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
fr: 第一段：兼职的质量差异很大
第二段：有价值的兼职特征
第三段：低价值兼职的代价 + 建议
items.es:
Should students take part-time jobs? The question cannot be answered without asking what kind of job, because part-time work ranges from tutoring that reinforces a subject to unpaid labour in a shop that teaches only endurance.

A good part-time job has two features: it develops a skill the student wants, and it pays enough to be worth the hours. Tutoring, translation, laboratory assistance and internships in a target industry all meet this test.

A poor part-time job consumes the hours that should go into study and returns money at a rate that will look small after graduation. The hidden cost is opportunity: the reading not done, the project not joined, the sleep not taken.

The reasonable rule is a ceiling — no more than twelve hours a week during term — and a purpose. If the job cannot be described in one sentence that would interest an employer or a supervisor, it is probably time sold too cheaply.
ph: ranges from A to B 从 A 到 B 不等
meet this test 满足这一标准
The hidden cost is opportunity 隐性成本是机会
a ceiling 上限

items.dir: Directions: Some travellers prefer package tours, others prefer independent travel. Which do you prefer? Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 比较两种方式的核心差异
给出自己的选择与理由
fr: 第一段：不选边，按目的地与经验判断
第二段：跟团的价值（效率、安全）
第三段：自由行的价值 + 我的偏好
items.es:
Package tours or independent travel? The choice should follow the destination and the traveller rather than a general preference for freedom.

Transport, tickets and language are handled, which matters in places where a missed connection ruins a week. It is also safer for inexperienced travellers and cheaper per day, because agencies buy in bulk. The cost is time: a schedule designed for forty people moves at the speed of the slowest, and shopping stops are rarely optional.

Independent travel is slower and less efficient, and that is precisely its value. A traveller who spends an extra afternoon in a small town because the light is good will remember it longer than a photograph taken from a bus window.
